newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX closes bourse trade up, banks rally.
newsitem.headline: German DAX closes bourse trade up, banks rally.

text.p: Germany's DAX share index closed bourse trade strongly up on Wednesday after renewed takeover speculation in the banking sector drove shares there to sharp gains.
DAX futures also moved well ahead and the dollar pushed up to 1.692 marks after Tuesday's widely-expected raise in a key U.S. interest rate, exerting a positive influence.

The DAX-30 index ended 68.98 points, 2.06 percent up at 3,418.12 after shares had seen early pressure following the Dow's overnight losses. June DAX futures traded up 44 points at 3,438.0 in mid-afternoon.

Banks were at the centre of market attention as dealers said the recent Krupp-Thyssen affair had caused a renewal of merger speculation in the financial sector and as Deutsche Bank, the largest German bank, detailed its 1996 results.

Early dealer fears that the market could go into reverse after Deutsche numbers were released proved to be unfounded as the bank reported group pre-tax profit of 4.9 billion marks compared to 3.6 billion last year.
Deutsche went on to trade 93 marks or 2.4 percent higher at 93.67 marks as dealers noted an optimistic outlook for the current year.

Dresdner Bank and Commerzbank, the second and third largest in the sector, also rose strongly among significant volumes, but the highest gains were seen in the shares of Bayerische Hypo, which traders said was being viewed as a potential takeover target.
They said that Dresdner, which has no notifiable stake in the mortgage specialist which is Germany's fifth largest bank, was being mooted as being interested taking it over.

Bayersiche Hypo rose 2.80 marks, more than five percent, to 57.80 on the IBIS electronic bourse by mid-afternoon. A spokesman for the bank said it had had no notification of any stake in it held by Dresdner.

Utility Veba fell 1.50 percent to 98.19 marks in IBIS after its 1996 results, which showed a group pre-tax profit rose 16 percent to 4.44 billion marks. It said however that future earnings growth was likely to be slower.

Steel and engineering group Thyssen managed to pull back most of early losses made on a continued reaction to the cancelled takeover bid by Krupp, which is due to make way for a steel joint venture between the two.
Thyssen shares ended just 50 pfennigs down at 375 in bourse trade after earlier hitting a low of 367.50.
Car-maker BMW rose 81 marks to 1,305 on continued positive reaction to more 1996 business details given at a news conference on Tuesday.
